jobs.prompt:
fix(cpp): port the production gateway changes made since the port was taken (DeepSeek compaction and a Sentinel repair)

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `agent-jobs/cppgw-combine-1-20261119-44443689630-1` of ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi. This branch contains ONLY the native C++20 gateway (`cpp/gateway/`: runtime layer `include/uos/rt` + `src/rt`, application under `src/`, vendored libraries under `third_party/`, 451 test binaries green on Linux ARM64 in release and under sanitizers) plus `static/` web assets. The original TypeScript gateway it was ported from is no longer in this branch; it lives on branch `development` (which is what production runs today) and at the pinned commit in `cpp/gateway/conformance/oracle-revision.txt`. Read `cpp/gateway/README.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` (driver: `bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh --config release|asan <test or --shard N/4>`) and `cpp/gateway/PORTING.md` (coroutine rules are mandatory). Your branch becomes a pull request; your final message is its body: a short plain-language summary for the owner.

OWNER POLICY (binding): generic functionality comes from mature open-source or standard libraries; less first-party code is preferred; the gateway's functional behaviour (wire formats, status codes, stored data, authentication and validation decisions, accounting) must hold and security must never get weaker.

GENERAL RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Run tests with an empty `HOME`, a fresh `TMPDIR` and no provider variables. No real provider traffic: use local mocks only.
- Do not edit `.github/` or anything outside `cpp/gateway/` and `static/`. Do not delete or weaken tests.
- Model connections can drop: create your report file in the first minutes and commit small steps often (the tree must build at each commit). Leave no build output, binaries or downloads in the checkout.
- Report file: `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/<job id>.md`: what you did, exact commands, real counts and measurements, what is unfinished, defects found outside your paths (report, do not fix). End your final message with the same summary.

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner (Ubuntu 24.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network). Its packages are too old for this tree: install Clang 21 or newer from apt.llvm.org (or GCC 14+), build Boost 1.92.0 `json` and `container` static libraries from the official source archive in a temp directory (the tree needs Boost >= 1.86), install OpenSSL 3, zlib, ICU, brotli, zstd development packages and build SQLite 3.54.0 as `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` describes. Bun 1.4.0 may be installed when you need to run the TypeScript.


HARD WORKING RULE: your process can be restarted without warning and then knows only what is committed. One change per commit, tree building at every commit, report updated in the same commit. After a restart read your report and `git log` first.

OWNED PATHS
- `cpp/gateway/src/**`, `cpp/gateway/include/uos/**` and `cpp/gateway/tests/**` as needed to port the changes below (NOT `src/rt`, `src/runtime`, `include/uos/rt`: other agents own the runtime layer), `static/**` if the TypeScript change touched the same asset, `cpp/gateway/docs/DEVIATIONS-FROM-BUN.md`, your report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-drift-port-20261119.md`.

TASK
Production still runs the TypeScript gateway from branch `development`, and it has moved since this port was taken. The native gateway must match production behaviour before it can replace it. `git fetch origin development` and list every commit on it that touches `src/`, `serve.ts`, `lib/` or `static/` and is not an ancestor of your branch (`git log --oneline HEAD..origin/development -- src serve.ts lib static`; expect about six, dated 2026-11-18/19). For each, read the TypeScript diff and its tests and decide:
- PORT: behaviour the native gateway lacks. Known ones: `fix(deepseek): compact at 75% of usable context`, `fix(deepseek): use one global compaction rule`, `fix(catalog): keep gateway DeepSeek window across metadata refresh` (the native constant is in `cpp/gateway/include/uos/deepseek/waterfall.hpp`; follow where the TypeScript value is consumed), and `Sentinel repair: issue 1281` (read it to learn what it changes). Implement the same behaviour in C++ in the corresponding module, port the TypeScript tests of that commit as C++ test cases (same inputs, same expected values), and update any recorded vectors honestly: if a vector file says it was recorded from TypeScript, regenerate it by running the TypeScript at `origin/development` in a `git worktree` with Bun 1.4.0 (local mocks only), not by hand.
- SKIP (owned elsewhere): the Antigravity / Gemini subscription commits (`fix(admin): preserve Antigravity sign-in and reset evidence`, `agent job agy-admin-meters-...`, anything about `gemini-quota`, `agy`, Antigravity): another branch (`codex/antigravity-gemini-subscription-20261118`) ports those. List them in the report as skipped; do not touch `static/admin.html` or `static/admin.js` for them.
- ALREADY PRESENT: say where.
Then update `cpp/gateway/conformance/oracle-revision.txt` ONLY if the paired conformance suite (see `cpp/gateway/README.md`) passes against the new `development` commit with the same two known shared failures and no others; otherwise leave it and report the differences. Record in the report, per commit: hash, title, verdict, C++ files changed, tests added.
Verification: the tests of every module you touched in release and `--config asan`; one full release shard; `python3 cpp/gateway/tools/links.py --check`. The hosted CI also runs when your branch is pushed.

DONE WHEN
Every listed `development` commit has a verdict; every PORT is implemented with its tests passing; the report states the `development` commit the native gateway now matches.
